name: Eastside Eats Command
description: 23 scouted restaurants, cafes and tea shops in Bellevue, WA and the surrounding Eastside.

restaurants.name: Dough Zone Dumpling House
restaurants.description: The one that started it all — right here in Bellevue in 2014, before it spread down the entire West Coast. Fast, loud, always a wait, always worth it.
restaurants.notes: Founded 2014 by Jason & Nancy Zhai. Now operating in WA, OR, CA and TX. The old Crossroads branch has closed — this Main St location is the downtown one.

restaurants.name: Me + Crêpe
restaurants.description: A tiny jianbing counter hiding upstairs in Bellevue Square between The Body Shop and Royce. Chinese street crepe folded to order with a crispy wonton cracked inside.
restaurants.notes: Four or five two-tops, that's it. Sometimes listed under the parent name 'Hi Duck'. Best solo lunch in the mall.

restaurants.name: CHICHA San Chen
restaurants.description: Taiwanese tea house that brews loose-leaf to order with a machine engineered to mimic a hand pour. This is the boba shop for someone who actually cares about the tea.
restaurants.notes: Founded Taichung 1998. Their Dong Ding Oolong has been recognized at the Brussels International Taste Institute. Relocated inside Bellevue Square in Feb 2025.

restaurants.name: TeaByDo (茶百道)
restaurants.address: 1075 Bellevue Way NE, Suite B-3 (Belgate Plaza), Bellevue
restaurants.description: Panda-branded megachain out of Chengdu that quietly became one of the biggest tea companies on earth. Cheap, sweet, extremely photogenic cups.
restaurants.notes: 8,700+ locations worldwide, founded Chengdu 2008. This is one of its newer U.S. beachheads.

restaurants.name: Tanoor
restaurants.description: Lebanese family kitchen baking its own pita in a tanoor oven on site — you can smell it from the sidewalk. The only place on this map where bread is the main event.
restaurants.notes: Third Tanoor location after Seattle's Dexter Ave and Sammamish. Opened downtown around July 2024.

restaurants.name: FOB Poke & Sushi Bar
restaurants.description: Self-serve poke and sushi sold by the pound in the basement of the old Expedia HQ. Build it, weigh it, eat it in eleven minutes. Best speed-to-lunch ratio downtown.
restaurants.notes: Seattle-area chain established 2017, roughly $14–16/lb. Note: this and the Belltown branch voluntarily closed for two weeks in late 2024 over food-handling concerns — worth a fresh look at recent reviews.

restaurants.name: The French Bakery
restaurants.description: Started in 2005 as a wholesale bakery and eventually opened its own doors. Croissants, macarons, and sandwiches on bread that is actually bread.
restaurants.notes: Three cafés now: downtown Bellevue, Crossroads, and downtown Redmond. The Crossroads location is a different address — don't get sent across town.

restaurants.name: Hokkaido Ramen Santouka
restaurants.description: Descendant of a nine-seat shop that opened in Asahikawa, Hokkaido in 1988 serving exactly one thing. The shio ramen is still the reason to come — milky tonkotsu, one pink pickled plum floating on top.
restaurants.notes: Order the shio, not the tonkotsu — it's the founding recipe and what the whole chain is built on.

restaurants.name: Din Tai Fung
restaurants.address: 10455 NE 8th St (Lincoln Square North, 1st floor), Bellevue
restaurants.description: Eighteen folds per soup dumpling, measured. Moved in April 2024 into a 17,000 sq ft space with a glass-walled dumpling kitchen you can stand and watch. Book 30 days out or accept your fate in the lobby.
restaurants.notes: CORRECTION: it is no longer in Bellevue Square — it's in Lincoln Square North as of April 2024. New space designed by Rockwell Group.

restaurants.name: Kobe
restaurants.address: 850 110th Ave NE (in the Courtyard Marriott), Bellevue
restaurants.description: A sprawling pan-Asian menu inside a hotel: sushi, teriyaki, hot pot, Korean BBQ and pad thai under one roof. Not precious. Perfect for a group that cannot agree on anything.
restaurants.notes: Open Mon–Sat 11am–11pm, closed Sundays. One of the later kitchens downtown.

restaurants.name: Story Coffee
restaurants.description: Independent and woman-owned, opened 2023. Real seating, real latte art, open-mic nights. The downtown café where you can actually sit down and stay a while.
restaurants.notes: Hosts community events including open mics. A rare non-chain in a downtown full of chains.

restaurants.name: Xiao Chi Jie (小吃街)
restaurants.address: 278 106th Ave NE (Urban Mix food hall, SOMA Towers), Bellevue
restaurants.description: Shanghainese hawker food run fast-casual, founded by a Bellevue native. The sheng jian bao — pan-fried soup buns with a crackly bottom — are the whole point.
restaurants.notes: Founded by Jennifer Liao and Caleb Wang with the owners of Just Poké. Also sells take-home xiao long bao kits.

restaurants.name: HEYTEA (喜茶)
restaurants.description: Shenzhen's 'new-style tea' giant — real fruit, salted cheese foam on top, glossy minimal branding. This was the first HEYTEA in Washington State.
recommendedOrders: Supreme Brown Sugar Bobo milk tea
restaurants.notes: Opened summer 2024 inside The Bravern. Get the cheese foam — it's the signature, not a gimmick.

restaurants.name: Mama Xita BBQ
restaurants.description: Despite the name: not Mexican. This is Chinese-Korean wagyu barbecue — 450+ locations across Asia, and this is the brand's first store in the United States.
restaurants.notes: Operated by Chubby Group; the brand runs 450+ locations in 31 Asian cities with 20+ years of history. The name fools everyone — tell Jimmy before he shows up expecting tacos.

restaurants.name: North — All-You-Can-Eat Dumplings
restaurants.description: Dumplings folded by hand on site, and $18.99 buys as many as you can physically hold. The correct answer to 'I'm really hungry and I have $20.'
restaurants.notes: Closed Mondays and Tuesdays. Not to be confused with 'The Northern Dumplings' on Bel-Red — different restaurant entirely.

restaurants.name: La'bean
restaurants.description: A brand-new Vietnamese coffee bar doing cà phê sữa đá properly, plus a handful of drinks you genuinely won't find anywhere else on the Eastside.
restaurants.notes: Opened 2025 in the Factoria strip. Free WiFi. The ube & peanut is the signature — order it even if it sounds strange.

restaurants.name: Sushi Omiya
restaurants.address: 3928 Factoria Square Mall SE, Suite B4, Bellevue
restaurants.description: Conveyor-belt sushi with a little monorail that drives your order to the table. Plates from $3.45. Objectively the most fun per dollar on this entire map.
restaurants.notes: Small regional chain with a second location in Tukwila. Free mall parking — rare advantage over downtown.

restaurants.name: Dough Savor
restaurants.address: 14505 NE 20th St, Suite M (Asian Family Market food court), Bellevue
restaurants.description: A Chinese breakfast counter inside a grocery food court. Youtiao and hot soy milk, jianbing, savory tofu pudding. The cheapest genuinely good meal on this map.
restaurants.notes: Inside the market food court, not a standalone storefront. Reviews favor the buns and pastries over the dumplings. Can get a long line on weekend mornings.

restaurants.name: Southern Spice
restaurants.description: Widely argued to be the best biryani on the Eastside. South Indian at the core with a North Indian menu bolted on and a daily lunch buffet.
restaurants.notes: Brands itself 'Southern Spice Bellevue' but the municipal address is Redmond, right on the line. The old E Lake Sammamish Pkwy location is closed.

restaurants.name: Seoul Meat Co.
restaurants.address: 12600 120th Ave NE, Suite 146 (Village at Totem Lake), Kirkland
restaurants.description: All-you-can-eat Korean BBQ with a grill built into every table. Two-hour limit, three meat orders at a time, no reservations. Show up hungry and early.
restaurants.notes: Roughly $39–45 per person depending on the day. First-come first-served — the Friday and Saturday queues are real.

restaurants.name: Kobuta & Ookami Katsu and Sake House
restaurants.address: 17026 Avondale Way NE, Unit A, Redmond
restaurants.description: Three siblings running a tonkatsu specialist and sake bar. The curry has dark chocolate in the sauce. The Seattle Times called it the best place in the region to pork out.
restaurants.notes: Family-owned by the Tandavanitj siblings; started on Capitol Hill before opening here. Reservations only for parties of 6+. Entrées run $21–34.

restaurants.name: Feast Buffet
restaurants.description: One of the largest buffets in Washington State. Sushi, dim sum, hibachi, Mongolian BBQ — and snow crab legs plus lobster claws on Friday through Sunday dinner only.
restaurants.notes: Lunch ~$27, dinner ~$39+, weekend crab dinners reported up to $45. It's in Renton Shopping Center anchored by Fred Meyer — not near a 99 Ranch.

restaurants.name: Champion Gourmet Taiwanese Cafe
restaurants.address: 18230 E Valley Hwy, Suite 122 (Great Wall Shopping Mall), Kent
restaurants.description: Taiwanese breakfast and comfort food tucked inside the 99 Ranch mall in Kent. The farthest target on this map and the one most worth the drive if lu rou fan is your thing.
restaurants.notes: Listed as 'Champion Gourmet' — your note said 'Champino', which appears to be a mis-transcription. Great Wall Shopping Mall has been running since 1999; make a grocery run while you're there.

restaurants.name: Pho Bac Cafe
restaurants.description: A no-frills mom-and-pop pho counter on East Valley Highway that people in Kent, Renton and Tukwila will argue has the best broth in the south end. Nothing fancy, nothing trying too hard — just the soup.
restaurants.notes: Open daily 10am–8pm (a few delivery apps list 10–9; trust the shorter hours). Despite the name, no connection was found to the Phở Bắc chain in Seattle's Chinatown-ID — this looks like an independent business. Cards accepted, private lot parking, no reservations, no alcohol.

restaurants.name: Happy Noodles
restaurants.description: Sichuan hand-made noodles cooked by owners who are actually from Sichuan. Huge portions, real heat, and a menu that runs well past noodles into braised duck, pork hock and hot pot.
restaurants.notes: Closed Mondays; Tue–Sun 11am–8:30pm. A rebrand of the old 'Noodle House' at the same address and phone. Most dishes run $13–19, hot pot $32.99. Sits directly across East Valley Hwy from Pho Bac Cafe, with Champion Gourmet a block south — three targets inside 200 metres, so Kent is worth one combined trip.
